annotation.title_clean: Chapter 837 — Aircraft Operation (Oregon Revised Statutes, 2025 Edition)
annotation.title_en: Chapter 837 — Aircraft Operation (Oregon Revised Statutes, 2025 Edition)
annotation.summary_en: Oregon Revised Statutes chapter 837 (2025) governing aircraft registration and operation, with a substantial section on unmanned aircraft systems (drones): limits on law enforcement use, public body registration and data policies, weaponized drone bans, privacy and trespass remedies, critical infrastructure protections, and state preemption of local rules.
key_provisions_or_claims: Law enforcement may not operate drones without a warrant, consent, or listed exceptions; unlawfully gathered evidence is inadmissible.
Public bodies must register drones with the Oregon Department of Aviation, file annual reports and publish data policies.
Operating weaponized drones is a misdemeanor or felony, with exceptions requiring FAA authorization, notice and $1 million insurance.
Drone flights over critical infrastructure, harassment of private premises and interference with aircraft are penalized.
State preempts local regulation of drones except in local government parks; property owners can sue for treble damages.
